Check

Check your download.

01 Is it the file we published?

Work out the file's SHA-256 and compare all 64 characters with the one on this page. If any differ, delete the file. A match shows the file is the one published here; the next check shows where it came from.

Linuxsha256sum veylor_0.9.1_amd64.deb
Macshasum -a 256 veylor_0.9.1_amd64.deb
WindowsGet-FileHash .\veylor_0.9.1_amd64.deb

02 Was it built from the public code?

GitHub Actions builds each file from a public commit of Veylor's code and signs a record of that build: the file's SHA-256, the repository, the workflow and the commit. With GitHub's CLI, signed in to any GitHub account, check the record:

gh attestation verify veylor_0.9.1_amd64.deb --repo ChinmayGopal931/vizor-fork --signer-workflow ChinmayGopal931/vizor-fork/.github/workflows/veylor-linux.yml

It fails unless GitHub signed a record of this exact file from Veylor's repository and its release workflow. To see the commit the file was built from, ask for the record's commit: it's the one the release is tagged at, listed with the files above.

gh attestation verify veylor_0.9.1_amd64.deb --repo ChinmayGopal931/vizor-fork --signer-workflow ChinmayGopal931/vizor-fork/.github/workflows/veylor-linux.yml --format json --jq '.[].verificationResult.signature.certificate.sourceRepositoryDigest'

This trusts GitHub's build machines, not us. Linux 0.9.0 came before these records and has none.

  • iPhone

    Apple encrypts and re-signs every TestFlight and App Store app, so nobody can compare the app on a phone with its source.

  • Mac, coming soon

    Signed by Zapp LLC and notarized by Apple. macOS checks both before it opens the app: keep Gatekeeper on.

Versions

Every release, with its notes.

Linuxv0.9.1Nov 21, 2026Attested

Release on GitHub · tag veylor-linux/v0.9.1 at d9c0ae1a5

Veylor for Linux, in beta: a private Zcash wallet, a fork of Vizor, with a new neon look and Shielded USD, a private dollar balance you can bridge to and from shielded ZEC. From this release on, every file is built and published by GitHub Actions from the release's commit, with a signed record of that build, so you can check that what you download comes from Veylor's public code.

What's New

  • Settings can copy Shielded USD's failure codes (Shielded USD, "Copy failure codes"): a short record of what failed, kept on your computer, to send us when something goes wrong. It holds no amounts, addresses, keys or messages.

Check your download

  • Compare the file's SHA-256 with SHA256SUMS, all 64 characters: sha256sum Veylor-linux-x86_64.AppImage. If they differ, don't open the file.
  • Check where it was built, with GitHub's CLI: gh attestation verify Veylor-linux-x86_64.AppImage --repo ChinmayGopal931/vizor-fork. It confirms the file was built by this repository's Linux workflow, and shows the commit it was built from: the one this release is tagged at.

Which file to download

  • Ubuntu or Debian: the .deb. It installs Veylor to /opt/veylor, with the permission Ubuntu 23.10 and later require for Shielded USD's protected page. Install it with sudo apt install ./veylor_0.9.1_amd64.deb (or the arm64 file on an ARM computer).
  • Other distributions: the AppImage. Make it executable and run it. On Ubuntu 23.10 and later, Shielded USD stays hidden in the AppImage, because Ubuntu only lets an installed app use the sandbox it needs: use the .deb there.
  • x86_64 and amd64 are for most PCs; aarch64 and arm64 are for ARM computers.

Notes

  • This is a beta. Start with small amounts.
  • Veylor needs a 64-bit system with glibc 2.35 or later, such as Ubuntu 22.04 or Debian 12 and newer.
  • Veylor keeps its secrets in your desktop's keyring (GNOME Keyring, or another Secret Service). If your system asks to unlock it, use your login password.
  • Shielded USD needs WebKitGTK 4.1 (libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0), which Ubuntu's desktop already includes; the .deb recommends it. Without it, Veylor runs without Shielded USD.
  • Shielded USD isn't available for Ledger or Keystone accounts.
  • Keep Veylor open, unlocked and visible while a bridge needs it. The bridge tells you when you can leave: with "Let the relayer claim for me" on, the default, you can leave a bridge to Shielded USD once the market maker confirms your deposit.
  • Shielded USD uses a public Ethereum RPC. To use your own, set it in Settings under Ethereum RPC.
  • Shielded USD's first sync can take a while. "Sync history from Anon's archive" in Settings, on by default, can shorten it.
  • Veylor on Linux doesn't update itself yet: download new versions from veylor.cash.
  • Veylor keeps its own wallet data, apart from Vizor's, so an installed Vizor is unaffected. To use an existing wallet in Veylor, restore it from its recovery phrase.
  • Veylor runs on Zcash mainnet.
Linuxv0.9.0Nov 21, 2026No build record

Release on GitHub · tag veylor-linux/v0.9.0 at f199881b0

The first public release of Veylor for Linux, in beta. Veylor is a private Zcash wallet, a fork of Vizor, with a new neon look and Shielded USD: a private dollar balance you can bridge to and from shielded ZEC.

What's New

  • Shielded USD: hold USDC privately on Railgun, beside your shielded ZEC.
  • Bridge shielded ZEC to Shielded USD and back. If a bridge can't complete, Veylor refunds it.
  • Send Shielded USD to a 0zk address, or withdraw it to an Ethereum address.
  • Receive Shielded USD at your 0zk address, or receive USDC on Ethereum at your deposit address. Veylor shields deposits while it's open and unlocked.
  • Shielded USD payments and bridges appear in Home's recent activity and in Activity.
  • A new look: true black and neon red, with your balance as a lit sign and sync progress as a line of light.

Which file to download

  • Ubuntu or Debian: the .deb. It installs Veylor to /opt/veylor, with the permission Ubuntu 23.10 and later require for Shielded USD's protected page. Install it with sudo apt install ./veylor_0.9.0_amd64.deb (or the arm64 file on an ARM computer).
  • Other distributions: the AppImage. Make it executable and run it. On Ubuntu 23.10 and later, Shielded USD stays hidden in the AppImage, because Ubuntu only lets an installed app use the sandbox it needs: use the .deb there.
  • x86_64 and amd64 are for most PCs; aarch64 and arm64 are for ARM computers.

Notes

  • This is a beta. Start with small amounts.
  • Veylor needs a 64-bit system with glibc 2.35 or later, such as Ubuntu 22.04 or Debian 12 and newer.
  • Veylor keeps its secrets in your desktop's keyring (GNOME Keyring, or another Secret Service). If your system asks to unlock it, use your login password.
  • Shielded USD needs WebKitGTK 4.1 (libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0), which Ubuntu's desktop already includes; the .deb recommends it. Without it, Veylor runs without Shielded USD.
  • Shielded USD isn't available for Ledger or Keystone accounts.
  • Keep Veylor open, unlocked and visible while a bridge needs it. The bridge tells you when you can leave: with "Let the relayer claim for me" on, the default, you can leave a bridge to Shielded USD once the market maker confirms your deposit.
  • Shielded USD uses a public Ethereum RPC. To use your own, set it in Settings under Ethereum RPC.
  • Shielded USD's first sync can take a while. "Sync history from Anon's archive" in Settings, on by default, can shorten it.
  • Veylor on Linux doesn't update itself yet: download new versions from veylor.cash.
  • Veylor keeps its own wallet data, apart from Vizor's, so an installed Vizor is unaffected. To use an existing wallet in Veylor, restore it from its recovery phrase.
  • Veylor runs on Zcash mainnet.
